observed./mnt/d/ClaudeWork/rimmandrake/art_eval/r: A clump of dark green fern fronds on a transparent background. All the fronds rise from a tight base low on the left of centre and arch over to the right, so the whole plant leans and fans one way, like a combed crest. Each frond has a pale, cream-green midrib running its length. The leaflets are narrow and pointed, densely set, and their edges are lit a little lighter. Several young fiddlehead curls sit at the tips on the left side. The shading is painterly and fairly realistic, with a thin darker edge. There is no soil, rock or shadow, and nothing is cut off. The plant fills most of the canvas, with some empty space at the lower right under the arching fronds.

At max zoom the fern stands in one cell beside the human and is roughly half to two-thirds of the human's height, with the base near the bottom of its cell and the fronds sweeping right. At 32 px/cell it shows as a small dark-green feathery tuft that leans to one side: readable as a fern-like plant, but the pale midribs mostly disappear. At 18 px/cell zoomed out it is a small green smudge. It reads as a modest bush or undergrowth plant.

Their hooked shapes extend the leaf silhouettes; the description requires drip-points, not visible water droplets. Small pale droplets becoming indistinct at normal zoom does not establish that the defining tip shape is missing.

request.prompt: A single shin-high tuft of the plant Dewblade for a RimWorld top-down-angled sprite, painterly vanilla RimWorld style, realistic, clean dark outline, transparent background. The tuft is a compact cluster of flat, broad strips of blade, each one a rigid ribbon standing upright and edge-on, stiff and straight with only a slight lean. Every blade in the tuft points the same direction, in tidy parallel rows, aligned like iron filings in a magnetic field, so the whole tuft reads as combed by one steady wind. Each blade narrows at its top to a distinct drip-point, and a small clear bead of water hangs at the tip of several blades, catching a highlight. The foliage is a muted, cool grey-green with slightly paler edges and darker bases, matte and dry-looking apart from the water beads. The tuft sits centered on the canvas with a small soft contact shadow at its base, fitting within about 0.8 of a tile, with the full silhouette visible and nothing cropped. Reference: none; build the plant from this description alone.
